title: Skill-Lock Audit and Auto-Registration for Critical Source Files
desc: Auto-detect .cs source changes, map to required skills, verify harness:skill registration in CLAUDE.md, alert on missing protection. Runs via wk-skilllock-audit.ps1.
steps: DRIFT FALSE-POSITIVE (2026-07-03): wk-skilllock-audit.ps1 keeps its OWN hardcoded required-skill map (RequiredSkills hashtable) separate from CLAUDE.md's actual harness:skill text. When someone updates ONE side (e.g. swaps a skill in the audit map) without updating CLAUDE.md's matching harness:skill block, the audit reports MISSING even though a registration exists -- it is really a SKILL-SET MISMATCH, not zero-protection. Fix applied: for EyeCmdPipeClient*.cs (3rd skill wkfind-caller-hwnd-validation-3tier-pattern -> caller-window-rect-dpi-piping-ipc-extension-for-precise-chrome-placement) and *AppBotEye*.cs (2nd skill elevated-eye-admin-pipe-server -> eye-health-mousecca-storm), edited CLAUDE.md to match the audit's map. Before assuming a MISSING finding means truly unregistered, grep CLAUDE.md for the filename pattern first -- if a harness:skill block already exists, the fix is aligning the skill SET, not adding a fresh 3-skill block.

ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-07-04 (separate from the earlier SKILL-SET drift): Test-SkillLockInClaude (wk-skilllock-audit.ps1 ~line 64-89) builds its CLAUDE.md search regex by reusing the hardcoded map's raw file-path regex KEY verbatim (e.g. 'EyeCmdPipeClient\.cs' expects the name and .cs adjacent), but a CLAUDE.md registration written as a GLOB (e.g. 'csharp/**/EyeCmdPipeClient*.cs') inserts a literal star between the name and extension -- so the reused regex never matches and the audit falsely reports MISSING for an already-registered file. Fix: strip the '\.cs' suffix from the map key before building the CLAUDE.md search pattern, searching only for the base name substring instead of requiring name+extension adjacency.
